subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Freshwater lakes tend to have diverse aquatic plant communities with various species of algae and submerged vegetation.
• This plant diversity provides a rich food web for fish, improving their nutritional intake and growth rates.
• On average, 78 percent of fish populations in freshwater lakes maintain stable numbers during seasonal changes.
• Coastal ponds are often dominated by single algae species due to high salt concentrations.
• On average, only 45 percent of fish populations in coastal ponds maintain stable numbers during seasonal changes.
prompt: The student wants to make and support a generalization about fish populations. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Freshwater lakes tend to have more diverse aquatic plant communities than do coastal ponds, which are often dominated by single algae species.
choices.B: Fish populations are more likely to remain stable in freshwater lakes than in coastal ponds because the diverse plant communities in lakes provide richer food webs.
choices.C: In freshwater lakes, nearly 80 percent of fish populations, on average, maintain stable numbers during seasonal changes, whereas in coastal ponds, only 45 percent do.
choices.D: The stability of fish populations depends on their nutritional intake, and diverse food sources are more available to fish in lakes than to those in coastal ponds.

explanation:
Choice B is correct. It generalizes that freshwater lake fish populations are more stable than coastal pond populations due to diverse plant communities providing richer food webs.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. While the sentence makes a generalization, it doesn't mention fish populations.
